summary.title: Linux kernel profiling with perf
summary.one_liner: You learn how to use the Linux perf tool to count events with perf stat, choose PMU, software and tracepoint events, and apply event modifiers and multiplexing.
keywords: count cpu cycles and instructions on linux
how to measure cache misses with perf
takeaways: perf stat runs a command and prints aggregated event counts at the end, e.g. perf stat -B dd ...
Events come from three sources: software events (e.g. context-switches), PMU hardware events (vendor-specific, e.g. cycles), and tracepoints from ftrace
Modifiers such as :u, :k, :uk restrict counting to user, kernel, or both privilege levels
When there are more events than hardware counters, the kernel multiplexes them and scales counts by time_enabled/time_running, which is an estimate
summary.summary: This tutorial walks through the perf profiler on Linux using worked examples from an Ubuntu 11.04 system with kernel 2.6.38 on an Intel Core2 CPU. It lists the perf subcommands (stat, record, report, annotate and others) and the options for perf stat. It then explains the categories of measurable events and how to list them with perf list. Finally it covers counting with perf stat, event modifiers, raw hardware event codes, and how the kernel multiplexes and scales counts when there are more events than counters. The page text ends before covering perf record or perf annotate, which the listing mentions.
